name: application-health-check-grid
title: Health Check Grid
description: Service health tile grid — a status dot, service name, and status/latency text per tile — with a live-pulse animation on operational services.
useWhen: Showing at-a-glance operational status for several independent services (API, dashboard, webhooks, search) in a compact grid.
Each tile benefits from a quick metric (latency) alongside its status, not just a status pill.
Building an internal ops dashboard or admin health panel — for a public-facing incident page, pair with `status-page-board`'s grouped list instead.
avoidWhen: You need a grouped, scrollable list of many services with uptime history — use `status-page-board` for that denser, list-oriented layout.
There's only one service to monitor — a single `connection-status-pill` is lighter weight than a grid.
Status data isn't real-time and won't be refreshed — a static grid risks looking live when it isn't; label it clearly as a snapshot if so.
responsiveBehavior: Two-column grid by default; increase grid-cols via className on wider dashboard layouts to show more tiles per row.
accessibility: Status is communicated by both a colored dot and a text label ("Operational", "Degraded", "Outage"), never by color alone.
The pulsing animation on operational tiles is purely decorative (aria-hidden via the parent's lack of live-region semantics) — the status text is the source of truth for screen readers.
Latency or "no response" text gives concrete detail beyond the status word alone, useful context during triage.

variants.title: Health Check Grid
variants.description: Four service tiles: two operational with a live pulse, one degraded, and one outage with a highlighted red tile.
accessibility: Status label and dot color are computed together from a single typed status field, so they can never disagree.

variants.title: Health Check Grid (Dark)
variants.description: Health check grid adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Status dot and text colors are tuned to meet WCAG AA contrast against the dark surface.
